setup: Stand with your feet about shoulder-width apart and your toes turned out slightly. Hold the load where the exercise calls for it (on your upper back, in front of your shoulders, or at your chest) and take a big breath to brace your trunk.
steps: Sit down by bending your hips and knees together, keeping your whole foot on the floor. | Let your knees travel in line with your toes and keep your chest tall. | Lower until your thighs reach parallel, or as deep as you can go without your lower back rounding. | Drive up through your whole foot, bringing your hips and chest up together, and finish standing tall.
cues: Brace before you descend | Knees track over your toes | Push the floor away
mistakes: Knees collapsing inward on the way up | Heels lifting off the floor | Hips rising faster than the chest | Rounding the lower back at the bottom
note: Start with a load you can control for the full depth, and use safety pins or a spotter for heavy barbell work.

setup: Sit with your back and hips flat against the pad and your feet about shoulder-width on the platform. Release the safety handles once the load is in your hands' control.
steps: Lower the platform by bending your knees toward your chest under control. | Stop when your knees are around 90 degrees, or just before your hips start to curl off the pad. | Press through your mid-foot and heels until your legs are almost straight. | Pause briefly, then repeat without locking your knees out hard.
cues: Hips stay on the seat | Knees follow your toes | Smooth turnaround
mistakes: Letting the pelvis tuck under at the bottom | Locking the knees hard at the top | Bouncing out of the bottom | Placing your hands on your knees to push
note: Move your feet higher on the platform to bias the glutes and hamstrings, and lower to bias the quads.

setup: Stand tall holding the load as the exercise calls for. Take a long enough stride that your front shin stays close to vertical at the bottom.
steps: Step into your stance (or set it) and lower your back knee straight down toward the floor. | Keep your front foot flat and your front knee in line with your toes. | Stop when your back knee is just above the floor or your front thigh is about parallel. | Push through the front foot to come back up. Finish all reps on one leg, or alternate legs.
cues: Straight down, not forward | Whole front foot stays planted | Torso tall
mistakes: Stride too short so the front heel lifts | Front knee caving inward | Bouncing off the floor | Pushing off the back foot instead of the front
note: Hold a support with one hand at first if your balance is the limit.

setup: Stand with your feet about hip-width apart on a firm, non-slip surface. Clear the space around you and wear shoes with grip.
steps: Drop into a quarter squat, swinging your arms back. | Jump as high or as far as you can, extending your hips, knees and ankles together. | Land softly on the balls of your feet, then roll back to the whole foot and absorb the landing by bending your knees and hips. | Reset your stance and repeat, keeping every rep crisp.
cues: Land quiet | Stick the landing | Reset between reps
mistakes: Landing stiff-legged | Knees collapsing inward on landing | Going for so many reps that quality drops | Jumping onto a box that is too high
note: Use a low box or jump height first. Stop the set when your landings get noisy.

setup: Sit back against the pad with your knee in line with the machine's pivot and the roller pad just above your ankles. Hold the handles.
steps: Extend your knees until your legs are nearly straight. | Squeeze your quads for a second at the top. | Lower the weight slowly back to about 90 degrees of knee bend.
cues: Sit tall, hips down | Squeeze at the top | Control the way down
mistakes: Kicking the weight up with momentum | Hips lifting off the seat | Knee out of line with the machine's pivot | Dropping the weight on the way down
note: Use a load you can lift with a smooth tempo; fast, heavy reps load the knee joint hard.

setup: Set the pad so your knees line up with the machine's pivot and the roller sits just above your heels. Hold the handles and keep your hips pinned.
steps: Curl your heels toward your glutes as far as the machine allows. | Pause for a moment at the top. | Lower slowly over two to three seconds until your legs are almost straight.
cues: Hips stay down | Pull with the heels | Slow on the way down
mistakes: Hips lifting to finish the rep | Cutting the range short | Letting the weight drop | Jerking the weight to start
note: The slow lowering phase is where much of the benefit comes from, so do not rush it.

setup: Stand with your feet about hip-width apart, knees soft, holding the load in front of your thighs. Pull your shoulders back and tighten your lats.
steps: Push your hips straight back so the load slides down your thighs and your back stays flat. | Keep your knees only slightly bent and your shins close to vertical. | Lower until you feel a strong stretch in your hamstrings, without your back rounding. | Drive your hips forward to stand tall, squeezing your glutes at the top.
cues: Hips back, not down | Weight stays close to your legs | Long, flat back
mistakes: Rounding the lower back to reach lower | Squatting the weight instead of hinging | Letting the load drift away from your legs | Leaning back at the top
note: For deadlifts from the floor, brace first and pull the slack out of the bar before the weight leaves the ground.

setup: Lie with your upper back supported (floor or bench) and your feet flat, about hip-width apart, with your knees bent. Place any load across your hip crease and hold it steady.
steps: Tuck your chin slightly and brace your trunk. | Drive through your heels to lift your hips until your torso is level from shoulders to knees. | Squeeze your glutes for a second at the top. | Lower your hips under control and repeat.
cues: Ribs down | Shins vertical at the top | Push through your heels
mistakes: Arching the lower back to get higher | Feet too far away or too close | Pushing through your toes | Letting the knees fall inward
note: Pad the bar or use a thick mat so the weight is comfortable on your hips.

setup: Set up on all fours, standing at a cable, or on a machine with the working leg free to move behind you. Keep your trunk braced and your hips square.
steps: Drive the working leg back by squeezing your glute, without arching your lower back. | Stop when your hip is fully extended and your thigh is in line with your torso. | Pause for a second. | Return slowly and keep the movement coming from the hip.
cues: Squeeze the glute | Hips stay level | Do not swing
mistakes: Arching the lower back to lift the leg higher | Twisting the hips open | Using momentum | Short, rushed reps
note: Keep the range to what your hip can do without your lower back taking over.

setup: Set the pad just below your hip crease so you can hinge freely. Hook your heels under the foot pads and cross your arms over your chest or hold a plate.
steps: Lower your torso by bending at the hips until you feel a stretch in your hamstrings. | Raise back up by squeezing your glutes and hamstrings. | Stop when your body is in a straight line with your legs. | Pause, then lower under control.
cues: Hinge at the hips | Squeeze the glutes at the top | Stop at a straight line
mistakes: Swinging up with momentum | Over-arching past straight at the top | Pad too high to hinge at the hips | Using heavy loads before the movement is smooth
note: Keeping the spine neutral emphasises the glutes and hamstrings; letting it round and extend shifts more work to the spinal erectors.

setup: Sit or stand so your hips are stable, with the pad or band around your thighs or ankles. Keep your torso tall and your core braced.
steps: Move your leg or legs out to the side, leading with the heel of the working leg. | Stop when your hip has moved through its range without your torso tilting. | Pause for a second. | Return slowly to the start.
cues: Hips stay level | Lead with the heel | Slow and controlled
mistakes: Leaning your torso to cheat the range | Swinging the leg | Rotating the hips open | Letting the weight stack slam
note: Lean slightly forward to shift more work to the glutes.

setup: Sit with your back against the pad and the pads on the inside of your knees (or use a band or cable at your ankle). Start the range at a comfortable stretch.
steps: Squeeze your legs together, or move the working leg across your body. | Pause for a second at the end of the range. | Return slowly to the stretch.
cues: Sit tall | Control the stretch | Pause at the end
mistakes: Starting too wide before you are conditioned for it | Using momentum | Letting the weight stack slam | Rounding the back
note: Build the range gradually, because the groin strains easily when it is overstretched under load.

setup: Stand with the balls of your feet on a step or platform and your heels free. Keep your knees straight but not locked, and hold a support or the load.
steps: Lower your heels into a deep stretch. | Pause for a moment at the bottom to remove the bounce. | Rise as high as you can onto the balls of your feet. | Hold the top for a second, then lower slowly.
cues: Pause at the bottom | Push through the big toe | Knees stay straight
mistakes: Bouncing at the bottom | Short, fast reps | Bending the knees to cheat | Rolling onto the outside of the foot
note: Bent-knee calf raises shift more of the work to the soleus.

setup: Sit with the pad snug on your lower thighs and the balls of your feet on the platform edge, heels free, knees bent about 90 degrees.
steps: Lower your heels into a deep stretch and pause for a moment. | Push up through the balls of your feet as high as you can. | Hold the top for a second, then lower slowly.
cues: Pause in the stretch | Full height at the top | Slow tempo
mistakes: Bouncing out of the bottom | Short range | Rocking the torso to move the pad | Rolling onto the outside of the foot
note: With the knees bent the large calf muscle goes slack, so this trains the soleus underneath it.

setup: Stand or sit with your heels on the floor and your toes free to move, with a light load or band on the front of your foot if you use one.
steps: Keeping your heels down, pull your toes up toward your shins as far as you can. | Hold for a moment at the top. | Lower your toes slowly under control.
cues: Heels stay down | Toes to shins | Control the lowering
mistakes: Bending the knees to help | Short range | Rushing the reps | Lifting the heels off the floor
note: Useful alongside calf work and for runners.

setup: Lie on the bench (or sit at the machine) with your feet planted and your shoulder blades pulled back and down. Hold the load over your chest with your wrists stacked over your elbows.
steps: Lower the weight to your chest under control, elbows roughly 45 to 70 degrees from your torso. | Touch or come close to your chest without bouncing. | Press up and slightly back until your arms are straight over your shoulders. | Keep your shoulder blades set and your feet driving into the floor throughout.
cues: Shoulder blades pinned | Forearms vertical | Leg drive into the floor
mistakes: Flaring the elbows out to 90 degrees | Bouncing the bar off the chest | Hips lifting off the bench | Wrists bent back under the load
note: Use a spotter or safety arms for heavy barbell work.

setup: Set the bench to 30 to 45 degrees. Sit back, get the weights to your upper chest, and pull your shoulder blades back and down.
steps: Lower the weight to your upper chest under control, elbows about 45 to 60 degrees from your torso. | Press up until your arms are straight above your collarbones. | Keep your shoulder blades set against the bench throughout.
cues: Forearms vertical | Press toward the ceiling | Slow, deep lowering
mistakes: Bench set too steep, turning it into a shoulder press | Flaring the elbows | Cutting the range short | Letting the weights drift apart
note: A steeper bench shifts work to the shoulders and away from the chest.

setup: Set the bench to a small decline and secure your legs if it has pads. Pull your shoulder blades back and down and hold the load over your lower chest.
steps: Lower the weight to your lower chest under control. | Press back up until your arms are straight. | Keep your shoulder blades set and your head on the bench.
cues: Control the descent | Shoulders pinned | Smooth press
mistakes: Bouncing the bar off the chest | Letting the bar drift toward your face | Flaring the elbows | Skipping a spotter on heavy sets
note: Unracking from a decline is awkward; use a spotter or a lift-off.

setup: Place your hands slightly wider than your shoulders (or as the variation calls for) and set your body in a straight line from head to heels, with your glutes and abs tight.
steps: Lower your chest toward the floor, elbows about 45 degrees from your body. | Stop just above the floor or when your chest touches the support. | Press back up to straight arms, keeping your body in one line.
cues: Body moves as one plank | Elbows at 45 degrees | Push the floor away
mistakes: Hips sagging or piking up | Elbows flaring straight out | Half reps | Head dropping forward
note: Make it easier by raising your hands, and harder by raising your feet or adding load.

setup: Grip the parallel bars (or sit at the dip machine) with your arms straight and your shoulders pushed down away from your ears. A forward lean works more chest, and staying upright works more triceps.
steps: Lower by bending your elbows, letting them travel back rather than out. | Stop when your upper arms are about parallel to the floor, or earlier if your shoulders complain. | Press back up to straight arms.
cues: Shoulders down and back | Elbows point behind you | Controlled depth
mistakes: Sinking too deep with the shoulders rolling forward | Shrugging at the bottom | Swinging the legs | Half reps
note: Stop short of the depth where you feel pinching at the front of the shoulder.

setup: Set your arms wide with a fixed, slight bend in the elbows, shoulder blades pulled back, and the weight at chest level (dumbbells, cables or a pec deck).
steps: Open your arms until you feel a stretch across your chest, without letting your shoulders roll forward. | Bring your hands together in a wide arc in front of your chest. | Squeeze for a moment. | Return slowly to the stretch.
cues: Hug a big tree | Elbow bend stays fixed | Slow on the way back
mistakes: Bending and straightening the elbows so it becomes a press | Going too heavy to control the stretch | Shoulders rolling forward at the end | Opening the arms too far
note: Stop the stretch where you feel the chest, not the front of the shoulder.

setup: Set a bench to an incline, or set cable pulleys low, with a fixed, slight bend in your elbows and your shoulder blades pulled back.
steps: Open your arms wide until you feel your upper chest stretch. | Bring your hands together in an arc up and in toward your upper chest. | Squeeze for a moment. | Return slowly to the stretch.
cues: Arc up and in | Elbow bend stays fixed | Slow lowering
mistakes: Turning it into a press by bending the elbows | Going too heavy to control the stretch | Shrugging the shoulders | Letting the dumbbells clang together
note: Light weights and a full, controlled stretch work better than heavy swinging reps.

setup: Lie across or along a bench (or stand at a high cable) holding the weight with straight-ish arms over your chest or in front of you.
steps: Lower the weight back behind your head (or let the cable rise) with a fixed slight elbow bend until you feel a stretch in your lats. | Pull the weight back over your chest (or pull the bar down to your thighs). | Squeeze for a moment, then return slowly.
cues: Elbow bend stays fixed | Ribs down | Pull from the lats
mistakes: Bending the elbows into a press | Arching the lower back | Going too heavy to control the stretch | Dropping the weight behind the head
note: Keep the range where your shoulders feel comfortable.

setup: Set the seat or stand tall with the weight at shoulder height, forearms vertical and your ribs pulled down. Grip a little outside shoulder-width.
steps: Press the weight straight overhead until your arms are fully extended, moving your head slightly back and then forward under the bar if you use a barbell. | Lower under control to about ear or shoulder height. | Keep your glutes and abs tight so your lower back doesn't arch.
cues: Ribs down, glutes tight | Forearms vertical | Press up, not forward
mistakes: Arching the lower back | Partial reps that stop above the shoulders | Elbows pulled behind the body | Bouncing out of the bottom
note: Warm up the shoulders first, and do not press behind the neck unless your mobility allows it.

setup: Stand or sit tall holding light weights (or a cable handle) at your sides with a slight bend in your elbows.
steps: Raise your arms out to the side, leading with your elbows, until they reach about shoulder height. | Pause for a second. | Lower slowly all the way down.
cues: Reach out, not up | Lead with the elbows | Shoulders stay down
mistakes: Shrugging the traps | Swinging the torso | Going heavy enough that form breaks | Raising above shoulder height with the palms up
note: A light load with strict form works the side delts better than heavy swinging.

setup: Stand tall holding the weight in front of your thighs with a slight bend in your elbows and your ribs pulled down.
steps: Raise the weight straight in front of you to about shoulder height. | Pause briefly. | Lower slowly to the start.
cues: Ribs down | Smooth lift | Control the lowering
mistakes: Swinging the body to lift the weight | Raising above shoulder height | Arching the lower back | Using a load that is too heavy
note: Front delts already work in every pressing exercise, so you may not need many sets of this.

setup: Hinge forward with a flat back (or set up on a pad or machine), arms hanging under your shoulders with a slight bend in your elbows.
steps: Sweep your arms out and back in a wide arc, leading with your elbows, until they are in line with your body. | Pause briefly and squeeze your upper back. | Return slowly to the start.
cues: Push the hands wide, not back | Soft, fixed elbows | Shoulders stay down
mistakes: Shrugging | Using momentum | Bending the elbows so it turns into a row | Letting the torso rise
note: A light load and a clear squeeze beats heavy swinging.

setup: Stand tall holding the weight in front of your thighs with a grip about shoulder-width or a little narrower.
steps: Pull the weight up along your body, leading with your elbows, to about chest height. | Keep the weight close and your elbows higher than your wrists. | Lower slowly to straight arms.
cues: Elbows lead | Weight stays close | Controlled lowering
mistakes: Pulling above chest height if your shoulders pinch | Shrugging hard with the neck | Swinging the torso | Using a very narrow grip
note: Stop at a height that feels comfortable in the shoulders.

setup: Stand or sit with your elbow bent to 90 degrees and tucked against your side, holding a light weight, band or cable handle.
steps: Rotate your forearm out (or in), keeping your elbow pinned to your side. | Stop when the muscle at the back or front of the shoulder has worked through its range. | Return slowly to the start.
cues: Elbow glued to your side | Rotate, don't swing | Light and slow
mistakes: Elbow drifting away from the body | Twisting the torso | Going heavy | Rushing the reps
note: Use very light loads; these small muscles tire fast and should not be strained.

setup: Set up lying face down on an incline bench, or standing hinged, with your arms hanging and a very light weight or no weight in your hands.
steps: Raise your arms forward and up into a Y shape, thumbs up, keeping a slight bend in your elbows. | Draw your shoulder blades down and back. | Pause at the top, then lower slowly.
cues: Thumbs up | Shoulders away from your ears | Light, strict reps
mistakes: Shrugging as the arms rise | Going heavy so the lower back arches | Swinging the weights up | Bending the elbows a lot
note: Very light loads are enough for the lower and middle traps.

setup: Stand tall holding the weight at your sides or in front of your thighs with your arms straight.
steps: Lift your shoulders straight up toward your ears as high as you can. | Hold the top for a second. | Lower slowly to a full stretch.
cues: Straight up, straight down | Arms are just hooks | Pause at the top
mistakes: Rolling the shoulders in circles | Bending the elbows to help | Short, bouncy reps | Jutting the head forward
note: Use straps or chalk if your grip gives out before your traps do.

setup: Grip the bar or handle slightly wider than shoulder-width with your arms straight and your shoulders pulled down away from your ears.
steps: Pull your shoulder blades down first. | Drive your elbows down toward your ribs until your chin clears the bar (or the bar reaches your upper chest). | Lower under control all the way to straight arms.
cues: Elbows to your back pockets | Chest up to the bar | Full stretch at the bottom
mistakes: Half reps that stop short of a full stretch | Swinging or kipping | Shrugging up to the ears | Pulling behind the neck
note: Use a band or an assisted machine to build the strength for full reps.

setup: Sit or stand facing the cable or machine with your feet planted and your back tall, holding the handle with straight arms.
steps: Let your shoulders reach forward slightly for a stretch, keeping your back neutral. | Pull the handle to your lower ribs by driving your elbows back and squeezing your shoulder blades together. | Pause for a second, then return under control.
cues: Lead with the elbows | Chest up, torso still | Squeeze, then stretch
mistakes: Rocking back to swing the weight | Shrugging the shoulders | Pulling with the wrists and biceps instead of the elbows | Rounding the back
note: Keep the torso quiet; if you need to lean back to finish a rep, the weight is too heavy.

setup: Hinge forward to about 45 degrees or lower with a neutral spine and soft knees. Hold the weight hanging under your shoulders.
steps: Pull the weight to your lower ribs or upper belly, driving your elbows back. | Squeeze your shoulder blades together at the top. | Lower to straight arms under control without standing up.
cues: Torso stays still | Elbows back toward the hips | Neutral neck
mistakes: Standing up as you row to swing the weight | Rounding the back | Jerking the weight off the bottom | Letting the knees straighten
note: Brace your trunk first; the lower back works hard holding the hinge.

setup: Stand tall (or sit) with the weight at your sides, palms forward and elbows by your ribs.
steps: Curl the weight up without letting your elbows drift forward much. | Squeeze at the top. | Lower over two to three seconds to a full stretch.
cues: Elbows pinned | Full stretch at the bottom | No hip swing
mistakes: Swinging with the hips or lower back | Stopping short of straight arms | Elbows travelling forward | Dropping the weight on the way down
note: Lower slowly; the lowering half of the rep builds the muscle too.

setup: Sit at the preacher bench (or brace your elbow against your inner thigh) so your upper arm is supported in front of your body. Hold the weight with your arm nearly straight.
steps: Curl the weight up, keeping your upper arm against the pad or your thigh. | Squeeze at the top. | Lower slowly to nearly straight, controlling the stretch.
cues: Upper arm stays on the pad | Squeeze at the top | Control the bottom
mistakes: Letting the weight drop at the bottom | Lifting the elbow off the pad | Using momentum | Over-stretching the elbow with a heavy load
note: The bottom of the rep is the hardest part, so stop just short of locking out.

setup: Set an incline bench (or stand with your arm behind your body) so your upper arm hangs behind your torso. Hold the weight with your arm straight and shoulders back.
steps: Curl the weight up without moving your upper arm forward. | Squeeze at the top. | Lower slowly to a full stretch.
cues: Upper arm stays back | Full stretch at the bottom | Slow lowering
mistakes: Swinging the elbows forward | Using momentum | Shrugging the shoulders | Using a very steep bench with a heavy load
note: The stretched position puts the long head under a lot of tension, so use a moderate load.

setup: Stand or sit with the weights at your sides and your palms facing each other, elbows by your ribs.
steps: Curl up, keeping the neutral grip and your elbows pinned. | Squeeze at the top. | Lower slowly to straight arms.
cues: Thumbs up | Elbows still | Slow lowering
mistakes: Swinging the weights up | Elbows drifting forward | Turning the palms up part-way | Short range
note: The neutral grip puts more work on the muscles under the biceps and in the forearm.

setup: Stand tall holding the bar or weights with an overhand grip, hands about shoulder-width apart and elbows by your sides.
steps: Curl the weight up, keeping your wrists straight and knuckles up. | Squeeze at the top. | Lower slowly to straight arms.
cues: Knuckles up, wrists straight | Elbows pinned | Slow lowering
mistakes: Wrists bending back | Swinging the hips | Going too heavy for the forearms | Elbows drifting forward
note: Use a lighter weight than for normal curls; the forearms are the weak link.

setup: Sit or stand with the weight overhead and your upper arms vertical beside your head, elbows pointing up. You can steady the working elbow with your free hand.
steps: Lower the weight behind your head by bending only at the elbow. | Go into a comfortable stretch while the upper arm stays still. | Extend back to straight arms.
cues: Elbows point forward | Ribs down | Only the forearm moves
mistakes: Elbows flaring out to the side | Upper arm swinging | Arching the lower back | Going so heavy the range shrinks
note: Keep the weight clear of your head; a lighter load with full range is safer.

setup: Lie on a bench with the weight held over your chest (or just behind your head), arms vertical and elbows pointing at the ceiling.
steps: Bend only at the elbows to lower the weight toward your forehead or behind your head. | Keep your upper arms still. | Extend back to straight arms and squeeze your triceps.
cues: Elbows stay still | Control the lowering | Lock out and squeeze
mistakes: Elbows flaring out | Letting the upper arms drift backward | Using too much weight for the elbows | Bouncing at the bottom
note: Use a spotter or a lighter weight, because the load travels near your head.

setup: Set the pulley high and stand close with a slight forward lean, elbows tucked at your sides and holding the handle at chest height.
steps: Push the handle down until your arms are straight. | Pause at the bottom and squeeze. | Let the handle rise to about 90 degrees without the elbows moving forward.
cues: Elbows glued to your ribs | Only the forearms move | Full lockout
mistakes: Elbows moving forward and back | Leaning over the handle to push with body weight | Stopping short of lockout | Using momentum
note: Rope attachments let you spread the hands at the bottom for a stronger squeeze.

setup: Set the pulley high and hold the bar with an underhand (palms up) grip, elbows tucked at your sides.
steps: Push the handle down until your arms are straight. | Pause at the bottom. | Let it return to about 90 degrees without the elbows drifting forward.
cues: Elbows pinned | Palms up | Full lockout
mistakes: Elbows moving | Leaning over the handle | Using too much weight for the wrists | Short reps
note: Go lighter than with an overhand pushdown; the underhand grip is weaker.

setup: Hinge forward with a flat back, upper arm tucked against your side and parallel to the floor, elbow bent to 90 degrees, holding the weight or cable handle.
steps: Extend your elbow until your arm is straight behind you. | Squeeze your triceps at the top. | Return slowly to 90 degrees without the upper arm dropping.
cues: Upper arm stays level | Squeeze at lockout | Slow return
mistakes: Letting the upper arm drop | Swinging the weight back | Rotating the torso | Using a heavy weight that ruins the form
note: A light weight with a hard squeeze at the top works best.

setup: Sit with your forearm resting on your thigh or a bench, palm up and wrist just past the edge, holding a light weight.
steps: Let the weight roll toward your fingertips and lower your wrist. | Curl your wrist up as high as you can, squeezing your forearm. | Lower slowly.
cues: Forearm stays flat | Full range | Slow lowering
mistakes: Lifting the forearm off the support | Going so heavy the range shrinks | Rushing the reps | Letting the weight drop
note: For the back of the forearm, turn your palm down and do reverse wrist curls.

setup: Sit with your forearm resting on your thigh or a bench, palm down and wrist just past the edge, holding a light weight.
steps: Lower the weight by letting your wrist bend down. | Lift it by extending your wrist as high as you can. | Hold briefly, then lower slowly.
cues: Forearm stays flat | Light and slow | Full range
mistakes: Lifting the forearm | Using too much weight | Jerking the weight up | Short range
note: Use a very light load; the muscles on the back of the forearm are small.

setup: Sit or stand with your elbow bent to 90 degrees at your side, holding a light weight or a bar by one end with your thumb up.
steps: Slowly rotate your palm to face down. | Rotate back through thumb-up to palm-up. | Keep your elbow still so only the forearm turns.
cues: Elbow pinned | Slow both ways | Light weight
mistakes: Moving the shoulder to help | Using a weight so heavy the turn gets jerky | Rushing the reps | Letting the wrist bend
note: Hold the weight further from the end to make it harder.

setup: Hold the bar, handles or hang with a firm, full grip, shoulders pulled back and down.
steps: Set your grip and brace your trunk. | Hold the position for the planned time or distance, squeezing the handle hard. | Put the weight down or release carefully when your grip starts to fail.
cues: Crush the handle | Shoulders down and back | Breathe steadily
mistakes: Rounding the shoulders forward | Letting go of the tension in your trunk | Dropping the weight from a long way up | Holding past the point your form holds
note: Chalk or straps help you extend the hold when grip is not the training goal.

setup: Pick up the weight with a deadlift motion and stand tall, arms straight, shoulders back and down.
steps: Walk with short, controlled steps. | Keep your torso upright without leaning or twisting. | Walk for the planned distance or time, then put the weight down with a flat back.
cues: Crush the handles | Tall posture, ribs down | Short, quick steps
mistakes: Shoulders rounding forward | Leaning or twisting | Dropping the weights with a rounded back | Taking big, bouncy steps
note: Pick a path that is clear and flat.

setup: Warm up thoroughly. Set your feet about hip-width apart, hands just outside your knees, with your shoulders slightly in front of the bar or weight and your back flat.
steps: Push the floor away and keep the weight close to your body. | As it passes your thighs, extend your hips, knees and ankles hard and shrug. | Pull yourself under the weight and receive it on the shoulders or overhead in a quarter squat. | Stand up fully, then return the weight to the floor under control.
cues: Weight stays close | Jump and shrug | Fast elbows
mistakes: Pulling with the arms too early | The weight swinging away from your body | Catching with your weight on the wrists | Hips rising before the shoulders
note: This is a technical lift. Learn it from the hang with an empty bar and consider a session with a coach.

setup: Set the sled with a load you can move with good form. Hold the handles or harness with your torso leaning slightly into it.
steps: Lean into the handles and drive through your legs with powerful steps. | Keep your back flat and your arms firm. | Push or pull for the planned distance, then rest and reset.
cues: Drive through the floor | Flat back | Quick, strong steps
mistakes: Rounding the back | Stopping the legs and arms taking over | Using a load so heavy you shuffle | Standing too upright
note: Reverse and backward drags are easy on the knees.

setup: Start lying or kneeling with the weight held steady, usually with one arm straight above you and your eyes on the weight.
steps: Move through each stage deliberately, keeping your arm vertical and your eyes on the weight. | Reach the standing or finish position with control. | Reverse the steps, returning to the start. | Repeat on the other side.
cues: Eyes on the weight | Arm stays vertical | Slow and deliberate
mistakes: Rushing between stages | Letting the arm drift forward | Using a weight too heavy for the whole sequence | Looking away from the weight
note: Practise without a weight until the sequence is smooth.

setup: Stand with your feet about shoulder-width apart in a quarter squat, holding the ends of the ropes with a firm grip and a slight bend in your elbows.
steps: Move the ropes in the pattern for the exercise, using your whole arm and shoulders. | Keep your legs bent and your trunk braced. | Work for the planned time, then rest.
cues: Quarter squat stance | Brace your trunk | Keep a steady rhythm
mistakes: Standing upright | Letting the lower back round | Only moving your hands | Holding your breath
note: Short intervals with full rest work well.

setup: Stand with your feet about shoulder-width apart, holding the ball at your chest or overhead. Make sure the space or wall is clear.
steps: Load by bending your hips and knees. | Throw or slam the ball with a fast, powerful extension of your hips and arms. | Catch or pick up the ball and reset before the next rep.
cues: Power from the hips | Fast and crisp | Reset each rep
mistakes: Using only the arms | Rounding the back to pick up the ball | Slamming into an unsafe surface | Going for sets so long that speed falls
note: Use a ball that is safe to slam, and keep the reps low and fast.

setup: Lie on your back with your knees bent and feet flat (or use the machine or cable set up), hands across your chest or lightly at your head.
steps: Curl your ribs toward your pelvis, lifting your shoulder blades off the floor. | Pause for a second. | Lower under control without letting your head hang back.
cues: Ribs to hips | Slow and controlled | Do not pull on the neck
mistakes: Pulling on the neck | Using momentum | Lifting the lower back off the floor | Rushing the reps
note: Take deliberate reps; a well-done crunch is already a hard exercise.

setup: Hang from a bar, or lie on your back or sit as the exercise calls for, with your core braced and your lower back controlled.
steps: Raise your legs, or bring your knees toward your chest, in a smooth motion. | At the top, curl your pelvis slightly so your lower back rounds a little. | Lower slowly without swinging.
cues: Curl the pelvis up | No swinging | Slow on the way down
mistakes: Swinging the legs for momentum | Lifting the legs with no pelvic curl | Dropping the legs fast | Arching the lower back on a lying version
note: Bend your knees to make it easier.

setup: Stand with your feet wider than your shoulders (or sit or kneel as the exercise calls for) and hold the handle, weight or ball with both hands in front of you.
steps: Rotate through your hips and torso together, turning the weight across your body. | Keep your arms mostly straight; they are just levers. | Return under control and finish all reps on one side before switching.
cues: Turn from hips and ribs together | Arms are levers | Smooth and controlled
mistakes: Pulling with the arms only | Rounding the lower back | Going so heavy you lose control | Letting the knees twist
note: Choose a load you can rotate smoothly.

setup: Stand tall holding the weight in one hand (or set up in a side plank or side crunch position) with your core braced.
steps: Bend sideways from your trunk, keeping your torso in the same plane. | Return to upright, squeezing the side of your trunk. | Finish all reps on one side before switching.
cues: Stay in one plane | Slow and controlled | Squeeze at the top
mistakes: Leaning forward or backward as you bend | Using too heavy a load | Using momentum | Twisting
note: A single weight is enough; two weights cancel the work.

setup: Set up in the plank, rollout or crawl position with your body in a straight line, glutes tight and ribs pulled down.
steps: Brace your trunk and hold your body in a straight line. | Move through the exercise (roll out, hold, or move your limbs) without letting your lower back sag. | Return to the start under control.
cues: Ribs down | Glutes tight | Straight line
mistakes: Letting the hips sag | Arching the lower back | Rushing the movement | Holding the breath for a long time
note: Shorten the lever (roll out less far, or hold from the knees) if your back sags.

setup: Lie or sit as the exercise calls for, with a light plate, band or harness. Keep the load light and your movement slow.
steps: Move your head through a comfortable, controlled range. | Pause briefly at the end of the range. | Return slowly. | Train each direction the same way.
cues: Start very light | Slow and controlled | Pain-free range
mistakes: Going heavy too soon | Jerking the head | Pushing into a painful range | Holding your breath
note: The neck adapts well but is irritated by sudden jumps in load.

setup: Choose a position where you can relax your body and breathe slowly. Warm up first, and ease into the stretch.
steps: Move into the position until you feel a gentle stretch in the target area. | Hold it, breathing slowly, for 20 to 40 seconds. | Release slowly and repeat on the other side.
cues: Gentle stretch, no pain | Breathe slowly | Relax into it
mistakes: Bouncing in the stretch | Forcing into pain | Holding your breath | Letting other joints compensate
note: A mild stretch feeling is the goal; stop if you feel pinching or sharp pain.

setup: Set up with a stable stance and a load you can control. Read the exercise name for the position and equipment.
steps: Set your position and brace your trunk. | Move through the full range of the exercise with control. | Return to the start without bouncing or swinging.
cues: Brace first | Controlled tempo | Full range you can control
mistakes: Using momentum | Rushing the reps | Choosing too heavy a load | Letting your posture collapse
note: Use a lighter load until you are confident in the movement.
